title: GPT-5 names caruncle oncocytoma from slit-lamp photos in two retrospective cases, months after histology, and gives a wrong leading diagnosis in three exploratory tests
summary: Given slit-lamp photos, ChatGPT (GPT-5) named oncocytoma first in two retrospective cases and gave a wrong leading diagnosis in three exploratory tests; patient care was not affected.
account: Sacchi et al. retrospectively analyzed two cases of caruncular oncocytoma. Both tumors had been excised, on 27 January and 26 March 2025, and confirmed histopathologically. On 8 September 2025, months after confirmation, the authors gave ChatGPT (GPT-5, 2025 version) only slit-lamp photographs and a brief summary (age, sex, site). They queried the model once per case and did not repeat runs. It proposed oncocytoma as the primary hypothesis in both cases. Differentials included papilloma, nevus, squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma. Perplexity proposed different leading diagnoses for the two main cases. The analysis had no effect on care. The authors published the report in Frontiers in Ophthalmology on 24 April 2026. They also report three exploratory tests using published images of other tumor types. GPT-5’s leading diagnosis was wrong in all three against the authors’ stated labels. The authors call the study a proof of concept that a general-purpose multimodal model can recognize a rare ocular surface tumor. They note that the small sample limits the finding. The authors declare no competing interests. These selected examples do not establish a rate of diagnostic accuracy. As of 29 October 2026, Europe PMC listed no article that cites the report.
